subject: Transportation Systems
title: Winglets and Fuel Savings
description: Learn Winglets and Fuel Savings in one minute.

hook.text: Look at most airliners and you'll see curved tips at the end of each wing. Those aren't decorative.

buildup.text: Air leaks from beneath the wing to above at the tip, creating drag-inducing vortices.

discovery.text: Winglets block this leakage, reducing drag and cutting fuel burn by up to five percent.

twist.text: Five percent sounds tiny. For an airline flying hundreds of planes daily, it saves billions of dollars.

climax.text: Modern designs like split-tip winglets capture even more savings from the same basic idea.

punchline.text: A small curve at the tip saves enormous fuel.

quiz.question: What do winglets do?
options: Reduce wingtip vortices and save fuel
